nodes.name: One-pot in situ hydrothermal sulfidation
nodes.procedure: Cobalt foam used as both hard template and cobalt source, phosphotungstic acid (PW12) as W and P sources, thiourea as sulfur source via thiourea decomposition (NH2CSNH2 + 3H2O → HS- + 2NH4+ + HCO3-). Sulfurization starts with reaction between defect sites of cobalt foam and HS- anions from thiourea decomposition. Relative concentration of cobalt/sulfur and PW12 introduction regulate synthetic kinetics for final crystalline phase, morphology, and composition of superhybrid Co3S4 nanosheet/P-doped WS2 nanosheet/Co9S8 nanoparticle metal sulfide nanoarray.

unit_operations.name: In situ sulfidation
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: Sulfurization starts with reaction between defect sites of cobalt foam and HS- anions

nodes.source_text: As illustrated in Figure 1, the synthesis procedure of superhybrid Co3S4 nanosheet/P-doped WS2 nanosheet/Co9S8 nanoparticle metal sulfide nanoarray (Super-Co3S4/P-WS2/Co9S8) was prepared through one-pot in situ hydrothermal sulfidation process with elaborate modulation of synthetic kinetics... The cobalt foam was used as both hard template and cobalt source, and the phosphotungstic acid (PW12) functioned as W and P sources.

The CoWSP only requires... 70 mV in acid... to obtain the current density of 10 mA cm⁻²... Tafel slope values of... acid-85 mV dec⁻¹... C_dl measurements... 56 mF cm⁻²... in acid... chronoamperometric measurements (i-t) curves demonstrate negligible attenuation... for 24 h

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD pattern (Figure 2a) shows peaks at 14.3°, 39.5°, 49.7° for hexagonal WS₂ (002), (103), (105) planes (JCPDS 08-0237); 29.8°, 39.4°, 47.7°, 51.9° for cubic Co₉S₈ (311), (331), (511), (440) planes (JCPDS 02-1459); 32.3°, 36.2°, 54.9° for cubic Co₃S₄ (200), (210), (311) planes (JCPDS 42-1448); absence of Co foam peaks confirms complete conversion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD pattern of Super-Co₃S₄/P-WS₂/Co₉S₈ is exhibited in Figure 2a. The absence of cobalt foam peak indicated the complete conversion into cobalt sulfide in the resultant Super Co₃S₄/P-WS₂/Co₉S₈. The existence of (002), (103), and (105) planes in hexagonal WS₂ (JCPDS card No.08-0237) can be confirmed by the peaks at 14.3°, 39.5°, and 49.7°. The strong signals observed at 29.8°, 39.4°, 47.7°, and 51.9° can be well matched with the (311), (331), (511), and (440) planes of cubic Co₉S₈ (JCPDS card No.02-1459). The diffraction peaks located at 32.3°, 36.2°, and 54.9° can be readily indexed to the (200), (210), and (311) planes, respectively, of cubic Co₃S₄ nanosheet (JCPDS card No.42-1448).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows uniform nanosheet array structure with planar size 2-5 μm, few-layer nanosheet edges, small nanosheets and nanoparticles decoration, strong substrate coupling.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images (Figure 2b,c) clearly recorded the uniform nanosheet array structure with a planar size ranging from 2 to 5 μm ... the decoration of several small nanosheets and nanoparticles can also be observed.

nodes.characterization_summary: Low-magnification TEM confirms composition of large nanosheet (Co₃S₄), small nanosheet (WS₂), and nanoparticle (Co₉S₈); Ac-TEM shows WS₂ (002) facet 0.62 nm (3-6 layers), Co₃S₄ (400)/(004) facets 0.23 nm at 90°, Co₉S₈ (100), (111), (-111) facets strongly coupled with WS₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The composition of large nanosheet, small nanosheet and nanoparticle in Super-Co₃S₄/P-WS₂/Co₉S₈ was confirmed by low-magnification transmission electron microscopy (TEM) image (Figure 2f). ... the lattice spacing of 0.62 nm is well in agreement with the (002) facet of WS₂, and the thickness of WS₂ nanosheet is presumed to be 3-6 layers.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX elemental mapping shows Co on large Co₃S₄ nanosheets and Co₉S₈ nanoparticles, W and P (3.1 at%) mainly on small WS₂ nanosheets confirming P-doping in WS₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) elemental mapping (Figure 2i,j) ... The distribution of P basically coincided perfectly with the distribution of W, implying that P element is mainly doped in WS₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co 2p shows Co³⁺ at 779.13 eV (2p₃/₂), 794.23 eV (2p₁/₂) and Co²⁺ at 782.16 eV (2p₃/₂), 798.34 eV (2p₁/₂) with ≈0.4 eV up-shift from CoS (778.7 eV) indicating electron transfer from CoS to WS₂; S 2p metal-S bonds at 161.8 eV (2p₃/₂), 163.0 eV (2p₁/₂), sulfate/oxidized S at 169.3, 170.4 eV; W 4f shows minor change with 3.1 at% P doping; P 2p at 132.2 eV (2p₃/₂), 133.3 eV (2p₁/₂) confirms P-W bonding.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The dissection of Co 2p signal in Super-Co₃S₄/P-WS₂/Co₉S₈ demonstrates the presence of spin-orbit doublets (Co 2p₃/₂ and Co 2p₁/₂) ... The high-resolution XPS spectrum of S 2p (Figure 3b) indicated the formation of metal-S chemical bonds due to two obvious peaks of S 2p₃/₂ and S 2p₁/₂ at 161.8 and 163.0 eV, respectively. ... the strong peaks of phosphorus element located at 132.2 and 133.3 eV were attributed to P 2p₃/₂ and P 2p₁/₂ signals, which demonstrated the successful doping of P in WS₂ via P-W bond.

nodes.evidence_snippet: The electrochemical double layer capacitance (Cdl) is also evaluated and shown in Figure 4g-i ... Super-Co₃S₄/P-WS₂/Co₉S₈ provides 69, 56, and 58 mF cm⁻² of electrochemical surface areas (ECSA) in alkaline, acid and neutral media, respectively, which is larger than 51/62, 45/51, and 22/45 mF cm⁻² of Co₃S₄/Co₉S₈ and Co₃S₄/WS₂/Co₉S₈ samples.
